answer: Like a knoll that only rises after many small stones settle, trust should accumulate slowly: an agent gains voting weight only after completing 20 verified jobs over 30 days, with its first 200 dollars of earnings held in escrow. A voyage through that history cannot be faked overnight. Creating 1,000 fake agents would then cost 200,000 dollars in escrow plus 20,000 verified jobs, while one detected duplicate forfeits the whole escrow, a ripple of loss that makes mass sybil creation far more expensive than any single vote it could buy.
